title: Theory of Kondo hybridization wave in Kondo lattice
abstract: Recent scanning tunneling microscopy experiments have discovered emergent spatially modulated Kondo hybridization wave (KHW) order in the heavy fermion superconductor UTe$_2$ and the artificial Kondo lattice system 1T/1H-TaS$_2$, challenging the conventional paradigm of spatially uniform Kondo hybridization in heavy fermion physics. Here, we develop a microscopic theory for KHW order based on the canonical square-lattice Kondo lattice model within the large-$N$ fermionic mean-field approximation. We systematically identify stable modulated KHW phases and establish their ground-state phase diagram. The prominent $\boldsymbol{Q}=(0,π)$ KHW phase yields uniaxial stripe modulation of the Kondo hybridization gap, which faithfully reproduces the spatial modulation pattern observed in UTe$_2$. Moreover, its inherent unit-cell-doubling modulation precisely accounts for the spectroscopic features measured in 1T/1H-TaS$_2$. We further predict a characteristic in-plane conductivity anisotropy that serves as a definitive transport fingerprint to discriminate KHW states with distinct ordering wavevectors. Our work provides a microscopic foundation for the newly observed KHW order and establishes a unified theoretical framework for understanding emergent modulated hybridization phenomena in heavy fermion materials.
summary: This paper develops a mean-field theory for the Kondo lattice to explain the emergence of spatially modulated Kondo hybridization waves (KHW). By modeling the order parameter with a wavevector $\mathbf{Q}$, the authors predict that the $\mathbf{Q}=(0,\pi)$ phase generates uniaxial stripe modulations and anisotropic conductivity. This provides a unified theoretical foundation for understanding these novel ordered states in heavy fermion materials.
main_problem: The paper addresses the experimental observation of spatially modulated Kondo hybridization wave (KHW) order in heavy fermion superconductors, challenging the assumption of uniform hybridization.
main_result: A microscopic theory successfully predicts the stable $\mathbf{Q}=(0,\pi)$ KHW phase, which yields uniaxial stripe modulation matching STM data in $	ext{UTe}_2$ and $1	ext{T}/1	ext{H-TaS}_2$, and predicts anisotropic transport as a fingerprint.
method: The authors developed a theory using the large-$N$ fermionic mean-field approximation applied to the canonical square-lattice Kondo lattice model.
model_or_system: The system is the Kondo lattice model, described by a Hamiltonian involving conduction electrons and local moments. The theory treats the Kondo hybridization order parameter $V_i$ as spatially modulated: $V_i = V_0 + V_1 e^{i\mathbf{Q}\cdot\mathbf{R}_i}$.
key_observables:
Kondo hybridization gap modulation (uniaxial stripe), in-plane conductivity anisotropy ($\sigma_{xx} 
eq \sigma_{yy}$), quasiparticle band structure, and Local Density of States (LDOS).
important_parameters: The ordering wavevector $\mathbf{Q}$, the Kondo coupling strength $J$, and the conduction electron filling $n_c$.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is the $\mathbf{Q}$-dependent ansatz for the hybridization order parameter $V_i$ and the use of the large-$N$ mean-field approximation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spatial modulation of the order parameter, the resulting four-band quasiparticle structure for $\mathbf{Q}=(0,\pi)$, and the corresponding DOS/LDOS features.
paper_structure: The paper develops the mean-field theory for the modulated Kondo lattice, derives the self-consistent equations for the order parameters $V_0$ and $V_1$, maps the ground-state phase diagram, and finally calculates spectroscopic and transport signatures for the key $\mathbf{Q}=(0,\pi)$ phase.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete, microscopic theoretical framework connecting abstract many-body physics (Kondo lattice) to specific, measurable experimental signatures (STM modulation, transport anisotropy) in complex correlated materials.
